title: Resumable Production promotion across offline local Staging and advancing main

phases.objective: Preserve an immutable governed Production candidate when local Staging is temporarily unavailable, record an exact resumable dependency, and automatically resume the same operation only after exact Staging Live Certification succeeds.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: A certified exact Production candidate reaches the required Staging Live Certification gate while local Windows Staging is stale or offline.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The controller records WAITING_FOR_STAGING without Production mutation and preserves the exact operation identity. After exact Staging convergence, the same governed request can be explicitly re-dispatched and reuses the existing candidate surfaces when all source pins remain valid.
steps: Keep the release cut, request head, Production SHA, candidate SHA, and review mode exact.
Treat only staging_live_certification failure as a resumable external dependency; all other supporting-gate failures remain hard failures.
Publish an exact staging-resume marker and resumable manifest with merge/deployment false.

Require current main to contain the authorized release cut, Production to remain pinned, candidate parent topology/tree to remain exact, and the request head to remain tree-identical to the release cut.
After Staging becomes exact, resume through the existing explicitly governed Production promotion dispatch using the same request identity; do not add an automatically mutating workflow trigger.
Register this critical E2E declaration exactly in Constitution.control_plane_paths and in the Derived State convergence automation control surface.
assertions: Advancing main with a descendant no longer invalidates the launcher merely because the trusted controller SHA differs from the older release cut.
No Production merge, deployment, migration, database mutation, provider mutation, credential payload read, secret output, or force push is authorized.
secrets_included is false.
Repository automation governance remains intact: no new workflow_run-triggered write workflow or implicit repository mutation is introduced.
The critical declaration is present in both canonical control-plane registries, so Policy Objection CI reports no changed-critical-path-unregistered blocker.

phases.objective: Exercise and govern the real offline-to-online Staging convergence path by allowing the current trusted local Auto Pilot driver to deploy an exact authorized Production release-cut ancestor without moving main or Production.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: A Production promotion request is in WAITING_FOR_STAGING with an exact GOVERNED_PRODUCTION_STAGING_RESUME_ARMED marker, while current main has advanced beyond the authorized release cut.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Start-AutoPilot keeps current main as the trusted control-plane driver, verifies the exact request head, resume marker, release-cut ancestry, pinned Production SHA and two-parent candidate topology, then permits only the exact release-cut payload to be fetched and deployed to local Staging. Production and provider authority remain unchanged.
steps: Require explicit AllowGovernedReleaseCutAncestor mode and a confirmation token derived from the first 12 hex characters of the exact release cut.
Verify the promotion request is open on main with the exact request head and exact control-plane title.
Require exactly one matching GOVERNED_PRODUCTION_STAGING_RESUME_ARMED marker binding request PR, request head, release cut, pinned Production and candidate.
Verify the release cut remains an ancestor of current main through GitHub compare evidence.
Verify Production still equals the pinned SHA.
Verify candidate has exactly two parents, release cut first and pinned Production second, and its tree equals the release-cut tree.
Verify the request marker is a one-parent direct descendant of the release cut with an identical tree.
Self-update the Staging control-plane driver to current main, not to the older payload commit.
Fetch and check out only the exact authorized release cut for the Staging payload, then continue existing exact-tree build-context and certification controls.
Leave Production merge, Production deployment, migrations, provider mutation, database mutation and secret output unauthorized.
assertions: Default Start-AutoPilot behavior remains fail-closed when origin/main differs from ExpectedCommit.
Historical commits that are not exact authorized ancestors of current main remain rejected.
A moved Production ref, changed request head, missing or duplicate resume marker, changed candidate parents, changed candidate tree or changed request-marker tree fails closed.
The operational resume path does not invoke gh workflow run, gh pr merge or git push.
The path grants only local Staging payload deployment authority and cannot mutate Production.
secrets_included is false.
The WAITING_FOR_STAGING resume marker must be authored by github-actions[bot]; user-authored lookalike comments are rejected.

Trusted resume-marker authority is parsed as exact key/value fields rather than by a whitespace-sensitive prefix, while duplicate keys, missing bindings, non-bot authors, moved SHAs, and executed markers remain fail-closed.

Trusted resume-marker discovery is independent of Windows PowerShell collection materialization: gh/gojq enumerates bot-authored candidate comment IDs across all pages, each comment is re-read as one JSON object, and exact field bindings remain fail-closed.

Trusted resume-marker discovery uses gh/gojq only to emit primitive id/login TSV rows; Windows PowerShell performs the exact github-actions[bot] identity comparison, then re-reads each bot comment and ignores unrelated bot comments before exact marker-field validation.
The current control-plane portable manifest is verified before any historical checkout; it protects the live driver, not the historical payload.

A governed historical release-cut checkout must be tracked-clean and is bound by exact commit/tree plus git-archive build-context provenance; stale historical generated manifest hashes are not treated as payload authority.
Non-historical exact-ref operation retains post-checkout portable-manifest verification.
Direct Start-AutoPilot environment bootstrap delegates to the canonical Initialize-StagingEnvironment helper used by One-Click instead of maintaining a second local secret generator.
Canonical Staging bootstrap fills missing Staging-only OAuth/MCP/activation secrets without exposing their values, while Production/provider/database mutation authority remains false.
Exact release-cut deployment bindings are applied only after canonical environment reconciliation.
Start-AutoPilot must not shadow Get-StagingEnvValue or Set-StagingEnvValue; canonical Staging-Environment owns tolerant reconciliation before fail-closed AutoPilot reads.

Exact Staging Docker builds may retry once only for recognized transient BuildKit frontend transport failures; deterministic failures or the second transient failure remain fail-closed, and recovery must not prune caches or remove builders.

Docker build stderr capture may temporarily relax ErrorActionPreference only inside the native Docker capture window, must restore the prior value in finally, and must classify success or retry from the native exit code rather than treating ordinary stderr progress as a script failure.
All long-running Staging Compose services run with init=true so PID 1 forwards signals and reaps child processes.

A zombie-container compose-up failure may trigger one Docker Desktop restart only when the zombie belongs to the current Staging Compose project and no non-Staging containers are running; recovery never removes containers, volumes, images, or cache.
After bounded isolated Docker Desktop restart, AutoPilot waits for Docker engine readiness and retries the exact compose-up once; any second zombie failure remains fail-closed.

Historical release-cut certification may use a pinned current-control-plane compatibility snapshot only when the historical report is blocked solely by runtime_integrity_verified; every other blocking failure remains fail-closed.

The compatibility verifier is read-only and may satisfy runtime integrity only through the current immutable-artifact proof bound to exact commit, tree, context-file-set SHA-256 and image digest; it performs no database, provider, ruleset or Production mutation.

After a successful compatibility proof, original readiness/degraded reasons are preserved and certification becomes degraded when any remain, or ready only when none remain; the temporary compatibility snapshot is deleted in finally.

Governed historical release-cut certification may additionally prove historical-app/current-Worker Activation Gateway compatibility only when the release cut remains an ancestor of the pinned current control-plane authority and the fixed Gateway runtime/trust source set is Git-blob identical across both commits.

Gateway compatibility is read-only: live /health must prove the current Worker exact source/build/bundle and canonical policy identity, while live /ready must independently prove upstreamReady=true, upstreamEvidenceVerified=true and upstreamSourceCommit equal to the historical release cut.

Local trusted-ingress evidence must be bound to the current Worker signing identity and exact returned public key/key id; the historical application identity remains independently bound by deployment-info and immutable artifact provenance.

A successful Gateway compatibility proof may remove only gateway_recovery_trusted_ingress, gateway_exact_commit and gateway_upstream_ready from degraded reasons; database/catalog/platform readiness reasons remain untouched.

The Gateway compatibility verifier performs no database connection, database mutation, provider mutation, Production access or Production mutation and never emits raw public-key or credential material.

phases.objective: Exercise main advancement, Production movement, repeated retries, and stale candidate branches with fail-closed behavior.
No provider or Production canary authority is added.
This change does not authorize Production merge or deployment.
